Context: This excerpt is from The Royal Charter of `text(1662)`, granted by King Charles II and explains the structure of the colony’s government under its new royal charter.
Title: Source 4: [Adapted from] the Royal Charter of 1662
Content: Several lands have been settled in New England. The trade and commerce there has been much increased. Therefore, we are pleased to make the settlers a political body. This body will have the following powers and privileges.

For the better managing of the colony, there shall be `text(one)` governor, `text(one)` deputy governor, and `text(twelve)` assistants who shall be elected by the freemen of the colony. We order that the governor shall assemble the assistants to advise on the affairs of the colony `text(twice)` a `text(year)`. `text(Once)` a `text(year)`, the governor, deputy governor, and assistants of the colony shall be newly elected by a majority of voters.

Further, all of our subjects who live in the colony and all their children shall have and enjoy all liberties of free subjects in England. We further grant the right to establish all manner of reasonable laws not opposed to the laws of England.
